rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tevdīʿ first means a departing guest's gracious farewell and prayers, then came to mean simply leaving; here it means leaving because farewell cannot literally be attributed to God.
rows.anchor: aslında misafirin vedâ etmesi, yani giderken kalanlara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation's occasion supports reading the verb as abandonment: God did not leave the Prophet out of anger, but through continuing mercy and care.
rows.anchor: Sebeb-i nüzûl de buna diğer bir karînedir. Yani bırakmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abandonment can express either grace or chastisement; the contrast of forenoon and night hints that the Prophet remains under divine mercy, while the denial of hatred excludes wrath.
rows.anchor: Duhâ ve leyl tekabülünde buna da işaret vardır. Bundan dolayı bırakılmamaktan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No human is left wholly neglected: under the responsibility of divine lordship, each is governed by mercy or wrath.
rows.anchor: hiçbir insan mühmel olarak ale’l-ıtlâk terkedilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads al-ākhira broadly as every later stage in the Prophet's life being better than its earlier stage, culminating in the afterlife, rather than only the hereafter opposed to worldly life.
rows.anchor: Ve her hâlde âhire bulunduğun her hâlin sonu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not mean that dying immediately would be better for Muhammad; that would wrongly imply his later worldly life brought no greater good.
rows.anchor: “şu anda ölmek senin için daha hayırlıdır” demek olur

rows.speaker: ابن عطية، müfessirîn
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya and other commentators take the verse as saying the end of Muhammad's affair is better than its beginning, with strength and rank continually rising.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye ve daha bir kısım müfessirîn bunu bidâyet ve nihâyet mânasıyla

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، رسول الله
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī and al-Bayhaqī transmit from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet was shown future conquests for his community, rejoiced, and then this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Taberânî’nin Evsat’ta, Beyhakī’nin Delâil’de İbn Abbas’tan tahric eyledikleri şu hadîse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future realization of the promise was shown as a vision, a miracle; the later conquests of the Persian and Byzantine realms and Constantinople are examples.
rows.anchor: Kisrâ ve Kayser mülklerinin ve Kostantiniyye’nin fethi hakkındaki haberler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators take al-ākhira in its familiar sense of the afterlife and al-ūlā as this world; he says this can fit the context if worldly life is also understood as blessed until death.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde diğer bir kısım müfessirînin dedikleri gibi burada da “âhiret” mâruf olduğu üzere “dünya” mukabili

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative hayr entails that worldly life is itself good, while the broader reading additionally conveys steady growth in good from one stage to the next.
rows.anchor: Bu mazmun “hayr” kelimesinin ism-i tafdil olmasından müstebân olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction for you contrasts Muhammad with hostile unbelievers; his believing followers share his hereafter's good, while even unbelievers benefit from his worldly good.
rows.anchor: lâm-ı ihtisâsın mânası da cemî‘-i mâ‘adâya nazaran değil, ezâ eden kâfirlere nazaran kasrdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening fa either draws an inference from the preceding favors or explains them causally, and also promises continuing relief; inna confirms that promise.
rows.anchor: فا fasîha olarak mâkablinden mâba‘dine istikrâ ve istişhad ile tefrî‘tarzında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although al-ʿusr appears definite and anaphoric, its meaning is universal: the known particular hardship opens onto the general rule that hardship is accompanied by ease.
rows.anchor: cüz’îden küllîye intikal ile hakikatte vaadi ifade için istiğrâka işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet's chest was opened, burden removed, and renown raised, his hardship already had ease with it, and further ease is promised.
rows.anchor: O şerh-i sadr, vaz‘-ı vizr, ref‘-i zikir madem ki oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated statement confirms the first promise and generalizes it: whoever confronts hardship with faith and patient endurance by God's permission reaches its ease.
rows.anchor: Bu da evvelkini teyid ve tekid olmakla beraber istînaf ile vaadden vaade ta‘mîm hâlinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿa can mean baʿda because hardship and ease succeed one another, as also expressed by the promise that God will bring ease after hardship.
rows.anchor: Zira usr ve yüsr ezdâddan olduğu için ictimâ‘ları câiz olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They can also be considered simultaneous from different aspects: what seems difficult from one angle may contain an easier aspect that can be found and acted upon.
rows.anchor: bir cihetten zor görünen bir şeyde diğer cihetten bir kolaylık vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who affirm the good and act accordingly have two kinds of ease in every hardship, one worldly and one otherworldly.
rows.anchor: hüsnâyı tasdik eden ve ona göre çalışan mü’minler için her usrda iki yüsr

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When the verses descended, the Prophet came out smiling and said that one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bu nâzil olunca ferah ve sürûr ile gülerek çıkmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar grammatical explanation counts one definite hardship and two indefinite eases, though the author also derives the point from the verses' links to their context.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna ekseriyetle “usr”un ma‘rife, “yüsr”ün nekre olmasıyla îzah edilmiştir

rows.speaker: Zeyd b. Eslem، Ebû Ubeyde، Ömer b. Hattâb
rows.claim: In a report through Zayd b. Aslam, Abu ʿUbayda wrote ʿUmar about the Romans; ʿUmar replied that God brings relief after hardship in a believer's heart and hardship cannot defeat two eases.
rows.anchor: İmam Mâlik Muvattâ’da Zeyd b. Eslem’den rivayet etmiştir ki Ebû Ubeyde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it a believer's heart points to faith's tranquility and patience; a believer's lamentation and loss of afterlife reward do not invalidate the promise, whose fulfillment remains subject to God's will.
rows.anchor: denilmekle imanın muktezâsı olan itmi’nân ve sabra da işaret vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although tīn literally means fig, he prefers retaining Tīn and Zaytūn as proper names when they designate places, since translating a proper name by its lexical sense misidentifies its referent.
rows.anchor: burada öyle terceme etmek pek muvâfık olmayacaktır. Zira müfessirînin birçoğunun beyânına göre

rows.speaker: حسن، مجاهد، عكرمة، إبراهيم النخعي، عطاء، مقاتل، كلبى، ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported view takes tīn and zaytūn literally as familiar fruits or their trees; the cited glosses call them the figs and olives people eat or press.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan, Mücâhid’den, İkrime’den, İbrâhîm Nehaî’den, Atâ’dan, Mukātil’den, Kelbî’den ve daha bazılarından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a contextual sign of metaphor, the evident meaning is the familiar fruits; their value as food, fruit, medicine, and trade may explain the oath.
rows.anchor: zeytin diye bildiğimiz meyveler olmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Figs and olives may represent important provisions generally, while Sinai and the secure city represent places of spiritual provision; the oath can thus encompass material and spiritual sustenance.
rows.anchor: ehemmiyetli me’kûlâtı temsil edecek birer misâl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two fruits may also allude to female and male, as the oath in al-Layl suggests; on this view they can be translated literally.
rows.anchor: bu iki meyvenin dişi ve erkekten kinaye olmaları ihtimâli de ba‘îd değildir

rows.speaker: birçok müfessirîn، آلوسي
rows.claim: Another view takes Tīn and Zaytūn as blessed places rather than fruit, supported by their pairing with Sinai and the secure city; al-Ālūsī favors this view.
rows.anchor: Âlûsi de “birçoğunun zâhib olduğu üzere bunlar mübarek, şerefli buk‘alara kasemdir”

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, as transmitted by Ibn Jarīr, identifies Tīn as the mountain where Damascus stands and Zaytūn as the mountain where Jerusalem stands.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr de Katâde’den: “Tîn”, Dımaşk’ın bulunduğu cebel, “Zeytûn” Beyt-i Makdis’in

rows.speaker: عكرمة، ربيع
rows.claim: ʿIkrima calls them two mountains; Rabīʿ locates them between Hamadan and Hulwan or among the mountains of Syria.
rows.anchor: İkrime bir rivayette de bunlar iki cebeldir

rows.speaker: أبو حبيب حارث بن محمر
rows.claim: A report identifies them as Mount Tīnā and Mount Zaytā, named for the figs and olives that grow well there.
rows.anchor: “Zeytûn” “Tûr-i Zeytâ” denilen dağlardır

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī attributes to Ibn ʿAbbās two Holy Land mountains: the fig mountain is Jesus's mission site, and the olive mountain is Syria, where most Israelite prophets were sent.
rows.anchor: İmâm Râzî bunu İbn Abbas’ın kavli olmak üzere naklederek şöyle der

rows.speaker: ابن زيد، كعب، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reported mosque identifications vary: Ibn Zayd says the Damascus and Jerusalem mosques; Kaʿb says Damascus and Iliya; one Ibn ʿAbbās report says Noah's mosque and Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd Tîn Dımaşk mescidi, Zeytûn Beyt-i Makdis mescidi demiş; Ka‘b da

rows.speaker: كعب، شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Town identifications also vary: Kaʿb says Damascus and Jerusalem, while Shahr b. Hawshab says Kufa and Syria; Kufa means the land where Noah lived.
rows.anchor: Şehr b. Havşeb de “Tîn” Kûfe, “Zeytûn” Şam demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He favors the sacred-place resonance: the familiar fruits and their productive lands, mountains, towns, and mosques evoke beneficial provision, righteous effort, and places where prophetic religion began; together they point to the Holy Land and a secure city.
rows.anchor: Bunlar da Tûr-i Sînâ ve Mekke gibi din menşe’i mübarek, şerefli yerler sayılmış olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tūr means a mountain, especially one bearing vegetation; Sīnīn is treated as the name of its region and appears in a plural-like inflection.
rows.anchor: dağ ve bilhassa nebatlı dağ, cebel-i zû-nebat demektir

rows.speaker: الأخفش، كلبى
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says Sīnīn is a plural meaning trees, with singular sīna; al-Kalbī glosses Mount Sīnīn as a wooded mountain.
rows.anchor: Kelbî’den de Tûr-i Sînîn, اَلْجَبَلُ ذُو الشَّجَرِ ağaçlı dağ diye mervîdir

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmit that Sīnīn means fine or beautiful.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’dan “‘sînîn’ hasen, yani güzel demektir” diye rivayet etmişler

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says that Sīnīn means beautiful in the Ethiopian language.
rows.anchor: İkrime’den de bunun güzel mânasına olması Habeş lisânı olduğu ziyadesiyle rivayet olunmuştur

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda describes Sīnīn as blessed, beautiful, and wooded.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr ve İbn Asâkir Katâde’den de “sînîn” mübarek, güzel, ağaçlı dediğini rivayet eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr prefers the recognized mountain name: if Sīnīn meant beautiful or blessed as an adjective, Tūr should be indefinite and take tanwīn.
rows.anchor: savab olan, Tûr-i Sînîn cebel-i mâruftur diyenlerin kavlidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the objection does not exclude the glosses beautiful or blessed: an omitted noun or lexicalized name can be in an annexation, and these qualities suit the known Sinai and its Quranic descriptions.
rows.anchor: güzel dağ demekten ibaret değil, mevzi‘inin veya otunun, ağacının mübarekliğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath over Tīn, Zaytūn, and Sīnīn can therefore mean the Holy Land, a fitting prelude to the account of the human being's best form.
rows.anchor: bu suretle o tîn ve zeytûn ve Tûr-i Sînîn üçüne kasem, arz-ı mukaddese kasem mânasında olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca by the commentators' agreement: it is the sanctuary containing the House and Abraham's Station and was made a place of safety and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn buna bi’l-ittifâk Mekke demişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report cited by al-Ālūsī calls it the site of the House that guides the worlds and the Prophet's birthplace and mission.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin zikrine göre merfû‘bir hadîste de

rows.speaker: قتادة، جمهور
rows.claim: The verse's being revealed in Mecca does not establish whether it preceded or followed the Hijra; Qatāda calls it Medinan if revealed after the conquest, while the majority calls it Meccan, possibly meaning its location.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den mervî olduğu üzere Medenî demek olur. Cumhûrun Mekkî demesi de Mekke içinde nâzil olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the conventional sense of Meccan as pre-Hijra, the security assurance suits the surah's setting and was given to the Prophet before migration.
rows.anchor: Mekkî olmakta meşhur olan mâna hicretten evvel olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amīn can mean trustworthy and free of betrayal; for a city, it may mean that it protects its inhabitants, or that its inhabitants are protected and unafraid.
rows.anchor: Beldenin eminliği de içinde bulunan kimseleri emin bir adamın emaneti hıfzetmesi gibi hıfzeder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca's security is tied to the Kaaba's divine appointment as a support for people and to Abraham's prayer for his descendants in the barren valley.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde emniyetli demek iki mânayı dahi ifade edebilir. Mekke-i Mükerreme’nin böyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's prayer was answered by making Mecca a secure sanctuary, drawing fruits to it, and protecting it while people around were seized; this supports the title secure city.
rows.anchor: duasına mazhar olarak أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَمًا ءَامِنًا يُجْبَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ ثَمَرَٰتُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's assurance also says the people will not be punished while the Prophet is among them or while they seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ahâlisinin hem Resûlullah içlerinde bulunduğu müddetçe hem de Allah teâlâ’nın mağfiretine tâlib olarak istiğfar eyledikleri müddetçe ta‘zîb olunmayacaklarına dair

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca's security makes it holier in this respect than contested Holy Land sites and creates an ascent in the oaths from material taste toward spiritual security.
rows.anchor: mânevî emniyet zevkine doğru yükselen bir terakki vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath teaches that homeland security matters and that a city's true worth is measured especially by safety, which is connected with religion.
rows.anchor: yurt emniyetinin ehemmiyetini ve yurtların, beldelerin kıymeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example of a once-safe, prosperous town that became ungrateful and tasted hunger and fear warns that security and provision can be lost through denial and rejection of a messenger.
rows.anchor: bu işaret وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًۭا قَرْيَةًۭ كَانَتْ ءَامِنَةًۭ مُّطْمَئِنَّةًۭ يَأْتِيهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar names Tīn, Zaytūn, Sinai, and the secure city evoke sacred places and their graded religious and worldly blessings, preparing for the answer about human creation.
rows.anchor: isimlerinin tanınmış olan ahid mânalarıyla zihinlere sarâhaten veya delâleten ifade ettiği bu mâna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the human species in the best form of bodily and spiritual shaping, ordering, and development; the phrase is a stable adverbial state of the human being.
rows.anchor: insan cinsini maddeten ve mânen doğrultmanın, kıvâma koymanın, biçimlendirmenin en güzelinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwīm means straightening, ordering, strengthening, or valuing; the indefinite wording intensifies the phrase to encompass every kind of excellence.
rows.anchor: eğriyi doğrultmak, kıvâma, nizâma koymak, kuvvet biçmek, kıymetlendirmek mânalarına gelir

rows.speaker: النخعي، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr reports that al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and Qatāda understand the verse as beauty of human form and senses.
rows.anchor: Nehaî ve Mücâhid ve Katâde suret ve havâssının güzelliği demişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported gloss is the straightness of the human stature.
rows.anchor: kāmetinin doğruluğu da denilmiş

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr b. Ṭāhir interprets the best form as adornment with intellect, understanding, and discernment.
rows.anchor: Ebû Bekir b. Tâhir akl ü idrak ve temyiz ile tezyîni demiş

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima understands the best form as youth and strength.
rows.anchor: İkrime de şebâbı ve kuvveti demiş

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr's preferred meaning includes every excellence, both bodily beauty and the capacities of intellect and character.
rows.anchor: evlâsı her ahsen olana umûmudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is a comprehensive sign that joins the unseen and visible realms and contains the meanings of the world's wonders and divine secrets.
rows.anchor: gayb u şehadet mecrâlarının mecma‘ı, ifade ve istifade felekleri neyyireyninin matla‘ı

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī says that a person's remedy and disease are within, and that the greater world is folded inside the supposedly small human body.
rows.anchor: İlâcın sendedir de farkında olmazsın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beauty is not merely outward form: it lies in feeling and recognizing beauty, knowing God as the absolutely beautiful, and acquiring divine character; this is humanity's intended perfection.
rows.anchor: insanın güzelliği ahsen-i takvîmde olması duygusuz olan şekl ü suretinde değil, duygusunda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are created with the capacity to rise toward this perfection, not born already complete; otherwise no mortality or lowliness would be observable.
rows.anchor: İnsan ilk doğuşunda bu kemâlde olarak değil, fakat bu kıvâma, bu kemâle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People begin with burdens and imperfections to shed: some purify themselves and rise, while many lose their share of beauty and sink toward the lowest ranks.
rows.anchor: birtakımlarının yükselmesine mukabil diğer birçoklarının da hiçbir hisse-i hüsnü kalmayarak en sefil derekelere kadar yuvarlanıp durduğu

rows.speaker: قاضي يحيى بن أكثم، الحنفية
rows.claim: A report says Qāḍī Yaḥyā b. Aktham and some Ḥanafīs ruled no divorce occurred when a man conditioned divorce on his wife not being more beautiful than the moon, arguing from this verse.
rows.anchor: Kādî Yahya b. Eksem ve bazı Hanefiyye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma ordinarily marks temporal delay; he rejects a purely rank-based reading if it means some people never shared the best form, since anyone called human must have some share of it.
rows.anchor: Bir insan denilince elbette ondan bir hissesi olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a time, God turns the human made in the best form to the lowest of the low, makes him most vile, or pushes him materially and morally toward Hell's lowest level.
rows.anchor: aşağıların aşağısına döndürdük, yahut sefillerin en sefili yaptık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent reverses purity, beauty, health, youth, knowledge, work, freedom, comfort, dignity, and pleasure into weakness, illness, ignorance, idleness, bondage, hardship, humiliation, pain, death, and Hell.
rows.anchor: Temizlik yerine eğrilik, güzellik yerine çirkinlik, terakki yerine tedennî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do righteous deeds in accord with God's pleasure are excepted: although bodily beauty may fade, they move toward salvation, absolute beauty, and a good final state.
rows.anchor: bunlar öyle merdud olmaz, o süfliyet derekesine düşmez, sûrî hüsnü, maddî kıvâmı zâyi‘etseler bile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is unending or free of obligation, continuing forever even when their bodies can no longer work and perish; they reach the culmination of the best form.
rows.anchor: onlar için öyle bir ecir vardır ki kesilmez, tükenmez veya minnet edilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oaths point to this rule: faith in the Creator, accountability, and righteous work for God lead to lasting reward, while those without faith and righteous deeds sink to the lowest state.
rows.anchor: İmanı olmayanların her ne yapsalar o sefalet ve süfliyete düşecekleri muhakkaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion is the law of accountability between God and people: humans submit in faith and good works, while God shows good and evil and applies reward and punishment; Islam contains both aspects.
rows.anchor: kullar tarafından fiiline göre cezâya inanıp iman ve amel-i sâlih ile selâmete ermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending of the previous surah, turn eagerly to your Lord, leads into the account of reward and punishment here.
rows.anchor: Onun için idi ki evvelki sûrenin âhirinde وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَب buyurulmuş idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what could make a person deny judgment despite its observable, rational, transmitted, and divinely promised evidence, thereby forgoing the lasting reward and risking degradation.
rows.anchor: artık sana dini ne tekzib ettirebilir? Bu hakikat böyle iken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses either any human exposed to the danger of decline or Muhammad, whose best creation and noble character make an accusation of falsehood especially groundless.
rows.anchor: Ey o ahsen-i takvîmde yaratılmış ve sonra esfel-i sâfiline red tehlikesine mâruz bulunmuş olan insan! Yahut yâ Muhammed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since human rulers punish rebels and reward obedience, the supreme ruler certainly enforces His judgment, distinguishing truth from falsehood and rewarding believers while condemning unbelievers.
rows.anchor: Hâkimler, hükümdarlar, isyan edenlere cezâ, itaat edenlere, iş görenlere ecr ü mükâfat verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns against assuming power makes one right or exempts one from punishment; people should fear God's judgment, uphold justice, serve the common good, and seek lasting reward.
rows.anchor: insan kuvvetli olunca haklı olur, her yaptığı yanına kalır, cezâ görmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verse warns unbelievers and gives believers good news.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle bu âyet, kâfirlere inzar, mü’minlere tebşirdir

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة، الترمذي، أبو داود، ابن مردويه
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says that after reciting this surah through the final verse, the Prophet instructed listeners to answer: Yes, and I am among those who testify.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî, Ebû Dâvûd ve İbn Merdûye Ebû Hüreyre’den rivayet eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Another report says that when the Prophet reached this verse, he would say, Glory be to You, indeed.
rows.anchor: Bazı rivayetlerde de Resûlullah bu âyete geldiği vakit سُبْحَانَكَ فـَبـَلَى derdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah establishes human creation and religion, summarizes the preceding surahs, and prepares for the next; beginning the next surah with Read in your Lord's name is fitting because religion is true and God is the best judge.
rows.anchor: hem evvelki sûreler bir hulâsaya bağlanmış, hem de bundan sonraki sûrelere bir temhid yapılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mughirāt can mean raiders moving swiftly, attacking, or plundering, and can also mean entering low-lying land; in common usage it chiefly means a raid or surprise attack.
rows.anchor: akın eylemek, yani sür‘atle gitmek veya baskın etmek, talan yapmak mânalarına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the verse as camels hurrying pilgrims to Mina in the morning, but enemy-raiding cavalry is the more immediate meaning.
rows.anchor: Deveye hamledenler, huccâcın sabahleyin Mina’ya sür‘atle gelmeleri mânasına anlamak istemişlerse de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dawn raid allows attackers to prepare unseen overnight and then see clearly, reducing mistakes; although night raids sometimes succeed, they are more dangerous.
rows.anchor: geceleyin düşmanın vâkıf olamayacağı bir surette tertibat alarak hazırlanmak hem de yaptığını yapacağını iyi görüp
